text:
Monzo is the better pick for most UK travellers because it offers zero-fee weekend spending and straightforward, unlimited card payments without needing to manage currency wallets. Revolut is only better if you plan to exchange large amounts of money in advance on weekdays or if you prefer holding a dedicated Euro balance to lock in a specific exchange rate before you fly.

Key Differences for UK Travellers (Standard Free Plans)
Feature	Monzo (Standard)	Revolut (Standard)
Weekday Card Spending	Unlimited fee-free (uses Mastercard rate)	Unlimited fee-free (uses Revolut rate)
Weekend Card Spending	Unlimited fee-free	1% fee on currency conversions (Fri 5pm – Sun 6pm ET) unless you already hold Euros
Fee-Free ATM Withdrawals	£200 per 30 days (in the EEA), then 3% fee	£200 (or 5 withdrawals) per rolling month, then 2% fee
Currency Holding	GBP only (converts automatically at time of purchase)	Multi-currency (can convert GBP to EUR/local currency in advance)
UK FSCS Protection	Yes (up to £85,000, full UK bank)	Limited (UK banking licence is in mobilisation/restricted phase; funds are safeguarded, not standard FSCS-protected like Monzo)
Which one suits your trip?

Choose Monzo if: You want a "set it and forget it" card. You don't have to worry about what day of the week it is, how much you've exchanged this month, or converting leftover Euros back to Pounds when you get home. Just tap and pay in the local currency.

Choose Revolut if: You want to watch the exchange rate and convert your Pounds into Euros on a Tuesday when the rate looks good. As long as you convert your money during the week and spend from your Euro wallet on the weekend, you avoid Revolut's weekend markup. (Note: On the free plan, exchanging more than £1,000 total per month incurs a 1% fair-usage fee).

Two Golden Rules for Both Cards

Always pay in the local currency: When a card machine or ATM asks if you want to pay in GBP (Pounds) or EUR (Euros), always choose Euros. Letting the foreign ATM or merchant do the conversion (Dynamic Currency Conversion) will cost you 3–7% in hidden markups.

Watch the ATM limits: Both cards cap free European ATM withdrawals at £200 a month. Since Europe is largely contactless, aim to pay by card whenever possible and save your £200 allowance for markets, tips, or cash-only spots.

(Note: If you are under 18, both Monzo Under 16s/16–17 and Revolut <18 have slightly tighter limits and require a parent or guardian to set up the account, though Monzo's 16–17 account still offers fee-free spending abroad).
